chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamdani (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of A'iz al-Ahmasi that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Four were given the hearing of all creation: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), the green-eyed Houries, Paradise, and the Fire. So there is no servant who sends blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and sends peace upon him except that it reaches him and he hears it. And there is no one who says: 'O God, marry me to the green-eyed Houries' except that they hear him and say: 'O our Lord, so-and-so has proposed to us to You, so marry us to him.' And there is no one who says: 'O God, admit me to Paradise' except that Paradise says: 'O God, let him reside in it.' And there is no one who seeks protection from God from the Fire except that the Fire says: 'O Lord, save him from me.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the four beings that hear all of creation according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith to illustrate the concept of 'sm' al-khalq' (hearing all creation) attributed to the Prophet, Houries, Paradise, and Fire, emphasizing the immediacy of divine response to specific supplications. This narrative underscores the Shia belief in the animate nature of Paradise and Hell as active participants in the cosmic order, directly responding to the believer's calls for union with the Houries or deliverance from the Fire. It serves as a theological reassurance that du'a is not merely a ritual but a communicative act received by these eternal entities.
